column1: # Accepted UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer sites, scoped to where they apply.
# A site firing outside its scope FAILS the round. A site absent INSIDE its
# scope is reported, but only after sustained absence -- because absence is not
# observation, and a fuzzer that never reached a site looks exactly like a site
# somebody fixed.
# WHY THE SCOPE COLUMN EXISTS
# PostgreSQL 18 rewrote tm2timestamp with checked arithmetic. Without a scope,
# every 18/master workspace reports that row withdrawable every round, forever
# -- a permanent false signal, guaranteed to arrive the moment those builds
# land. Scoping turns it into an assertion the gate checks in BOTH directions:
#   fires outside scope   -> a regression, or a backport nobody recorded
#   stops firing inside   -> a fix, or the target stopped reaching it
# The noise becomes the most interesting thing the list can produce.
# scope is a comma-separated list of workspace-name globs. "*" means everywhere.
# function
pg_strtoint32_safe
pg_strtoint64_safe
inet_cidr_pton_ipv4
inet_net_pton_ipv4
do_to_timestamp
# Rewritten with pg_mul_s64_overflow/pg_add_s64_overflow upstream; the 18+ and
# master trees should NOT produce it. If they do, that is a finding.
tm2timestamp
